Order No.06 Date: 01.10.2024
1.

The present writ petition has been filed for quashing the order as contained in memo no.771 dated 28th June, 2023 passed by the Additional Collector-cum-Arbitrator, Garhwa, NHAI-respondent no.4 in Misc. Case No.107 of 2022-23, whereby the said respondent has not considered the claim of the petitioners for payment of fair/adequate compensation with respect to acquisition of their land for construction of NH-75 (SEC-V) on the basis of market value in terms with Section 26 of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act,
2013.

entities.text:
Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act,
2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
Further prayer has been made for issuance of direction upon the respondents to pay adequate/fair compensation to the petitioners with respect to acquisition of their land for construction of NH-75 (SEC-V).
2.

Mr. Manav Poddar, learned A.C. to A.A.G.I, appearing on behalf of the State as well as Ms. Sweety Topno, learned counsel appearing on behalf of respondent nos. 5 and 6, jointly raise an objection with regard to maintainability of the present writ petition on the ground that the petitioners have got alternative/statutory/efficacious remedy under Section 34 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 to challenge the order as contained in memo no.771 dated 28th June, 2023 passed by the respondent no.4.
3.
Since learned counsel for the aforesaid respondents have raised an issue of maintainability of the present writ petition, it would be appropriate to deal with the same at the first instance.

4. Section 3-G(6) of the National Highways Act, 1956 [hereinafter referred to as 'the Act, 1956']
clearly provides that the provisions of the Act, 1996 shall apply to every arbitration under the said Act, subject to the other provisions of the same.

Thus, the impugned order as contained in memo no.771 dated 28th June, 2023 passed by the respondent no.4 in Misc. Case No.107 of 2022-23 has to be treated as an award passed within the meaning and the provisions of the Act, 1996.
The Act, 1956 does not provide any further Forum for challenging the award passed by an arbitrator under Section 3-G(5) of the said Act.

Thus, if any person is aggrieved with the award of an arbitrator passed under Section 3-G(5) of the Act, 1956, he has got the remedy to file an application under Section 34 of the Act, 1996 for setting aside the same.

Hence, this Court is of the view that the petitioners have got alternative/statutory/ efficacious remedy of filing an application before the appropriate Court seeking challenge to the order as contained in memo no.771 dated 28th June, 2023 passed by the respondent no.4 in Misc. Case No.107 of 2022-23.
5. The present writ petition is, accordingly, dismissed as not maintainable.

6. The petitioner is, however, at liberty to take alternative/statutory/efficacious recourse under Section 34 of the Act, 1996 against the impugned order as contained in memo no.771 dated 28th June, 2023 passed by the respondent no.4 in Misc. Case No.107 of 2022-23.
(Rajesh Shankar, J.) Arpit/
